delta: # Story 10 — Agent grants a customer sign-in from the customer screen (Story: CRM-66)

## Prerequisites

- **CUSTOMERS-4-API (CRM-63) completed** — `useCustomer(id)` at `web/src/pages/customers/useCustomer.ts:
36` already fetches the full customer screen (customer, tickets, notes) in one request. This story must not add a second fetch on scre

en load.
- **CUSTOMERS-6-API (CRM-65) completed** — Route registered at `api/src/features/customers/customers.routes.js:55` (`res.status(201).json(service
.grantSignIn(req.subject, { customerId: req.params.id }))`) and service method `grantSignIn(actor, { customerId })` at `api/src/features/customers/customers.service.js:137`. Confirm with the C
RM-65 plan the exact POST path (e.g. `POST /customers/:id/sign-in`), the response body shape (must include the plaintext initial password field, e.g. `{ userId, email

, initialPassword }`), and the `409` / `422` error codes so this story wires them into the shared error copy.
- **IDENTITY-2-API complet

ed** — supplies the underlying account creation the API story wraps.
- Coordinate with the owner of `web/src/pages/custom

ers/CustomerScreenPage.test.tsx` — that test asserts the customer is fetched exactly once. The new control must not add any request until the agent clicks the button.

---

## Story Go

al

On `web/src/pages/customers/CustomerScreenPage.tsx`, add a **Sign-in** section that lets an agent grant an account to a customer who does

not already have one.

User-visible outcomes:

1. If `customer.userId` is `null`, the section shows a **"Grant sign-in"** button. On click it
POSTs to the CRM-65 endpoint, disables while in flight, and on success replaces itself with a **single, plain, unm
asked** rendering of the returned initial password plus the account email. The password disappears on any navigation or reload of the screen and is never re-f

etchable.
2. If `customer.userId` is not `null`, the section renders a short statement (e.g. "This customer already has a sign-in.") — **no button**, because an action that will

be refused is worse than no action.
3. Field-scoped refusals from the API mark the offending field and render the sh

ared error copy from `t.errors[code]`.
4. The submit button cannot be double-pressed while a request is in flight.
5

. Every string comes from both `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` and `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts` (BR-6).

**Explicitly out of scope:** any change under

`api/`; any portal / self-service screen; persisting or re-showing the initial password after the agent leaves the screen.

---

## Product rules (from story)

- Owns rule **I-1**: users and customers are two tables; `customers.user

_id` is null until first sign-in. The web branch key is therefore `customer.userId === null`.

## Backend Tasks

**No backend changes required.** All API work belongs to CUSTOMERS-6-API (CRM-65).

---

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **
Customer already has a sign-in (`customer.userId !== null`).** Trigger: initial render. Expected: statement only, no button. Enforced in the branch inserted in `

CustomerScreenPage.tsx` between the contacts `Card` and open-tickets `Heading`.
- **Double-click during POST.** Trigger: agent clicks twice quickly. Expected: only one request;

button disabled while `signIn.status === 'loading'` (same pattern as note submit at `CustomerScreenPage.tsx:152`).
- **API returns 409 "
already has a sign-in" (race with another agent).** Trigger: two agents open the screen at once. Expected: error copy from `t.errors[code]` is rendered by
the `ErrorState`; **no** plaintext password is shown. The `signIn.status === 'success'` branch requires `signIn.result` truthy,

so a rejected promise cannot fall through to the credentials view.
- **API returns a validation refusal naming a field.** Expected: the field is marked (aria-invalid +

inline copy) and the shared `t.errors[code]` sentence is shown — no ad-hoc strings.
- **Navigation after success.** Trigger: agent cl
icks another link, or reloads. Expected: `signIn.result` lives only in the component; unmount discards it. Do not pers

ist to localStorage/URL/cache.
- **Screen reload via retry button (`ErrorState` `onRetry={reload}`).** After `reload()`, `useCustomer` re-run
s and `screen` changes; the `signIn` hook's local state is unaffected but the password view is inside the same
subtree — a successful grant, then a reload, must still not re-display the old password. `useEffect(() => setAdded([
]), [screen])` at **line 47** is the precedent for clearing local state when `screen` changes; add a similar effect for `signIn` if the executor conf

irms the plaintext survives across `reload()` calls.
- **RTL rendering of email / password.** Both are LTR runs
; wrap in `<Isolated>` as at `CustomerScreenPage.tsx:91, 94`. A password containing digits and punctuation would otherwise reorder in Arabic pa

ragraphs.
- **Hardcoded-string test on new separators or punctuation.** Any `·`, `—
`, `:` typed between tags will fail `no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` — use a module constant (see `SEPARATOR` at **line 28**) or move the pun

ctuation into the resource string.

## Test Plan

1. **Create file:** `web/src/pages/customers/GrantSignIn.test.tsx`. Mirror `web/src/pages/customers/InternalNote.test
.tsx`: render `CustomerScreenPage` inside a `Route path="/customers/:id"`, stub `fetch` per call, and cover the following cases.

Each stub must return a **fresh `Response`** on every call (L-30).
   - **Renders the button when `userId` is null.** After the initial scre

en fetch resolves, `t.customerScreen.signInGrant` is visible.
   - **Renders the statement, not a button, when `userId` is set.** Scre
en payload has `customer.userId: 'user-123'`; the copy `t.customerScreen.signInAlready` is present and `t.customerScreen.signInGrant` is not

.
   - **On click, POSTs to `/api/v1/customers/:id/sign-in` exactly once and renders the plaintext password.** Stub the second `fetch` call to resolve with `{ userId, email, initialPassword
: 'plain-123' }`; assert the password text appears verbatim, the email appears inside an `Isolated` wrapper, and there

is no masking (`•`, `*`) around the password.
   - **Double-click sends one request.** Simulate two

clicks before the promise resolves; assert `fetch` was called once for the sign-in path.
   - **Server refusal renders the shared error copy.** Stub the
POST with a rejection whose `code` maps into `t.errors`; assert the `ErrorState` renders that copy and **no** password field

is rendered.
   - **Field-scoped refusal marks the field.** If applicable (the CRM-65 API may not surface field refusals here — confirm with that plan;

skip this case if the API only returns whole-request codes).
2. **Modify:** `web/src/pages/customers/CustomerScreenPage.test.tsx`.
Update the fixture `SCREEN` object so `customer.userId` is set (or explicitly null) as needed by each existing case. **

Do not** change the "one request" assertion — the new control does not fetch until clicked. Rerun the file locally to confirm request counts still match.
3. **Modify (par

ity):** `web/src/shared/i18n/parity.test.ts` runs automatically; simply ensure every new key exists in both `en.ts` and `ar.ts` before running the suite.
4. **Modify (
hardcoded strings):** No test change needed. Run `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` — if any new `·`, `:`, or copy leaked into JSX liter

als, extract to a constant or resource string.
5. **Optional:** if the executor adds a `useEffect` that

clears `signIn.result` on `screen` change (see edge cases), add a test that reloads the screen after a successful grant and asserts the password is no longer visible.

---

## Migration / Rollback

No sch
ema or persistent-state change. Rollback is a code-only revert of the three touched files (`CustomerScreenPage.tsx`, `useCustomer.ts`, `use
GrantSignIn.ts`) and the two i18n files. A half-applied state (button rendered but API unavailable) surfaces as the shared error copy — nothing is written

client-side.

---

## Verification Steps

1. **Frontend runs:** `cd web && npm test` — must pass, including `GrantSignIn.test.tsx`, the unchanged single

-request assertions in `CustomerScreenPage.test.tsx`, `parity.test.ts`, and `no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts`.

s `tsc -b && vite build`; the `tsc -b` step is the only typecheck the story gets, since `npm test` (vitest) does not typecheck (

3. **Backend regression:** `cd api && npm test` — must remain green; no api change should

be needed, so any regression is a signal the CRM-65 contract shifted.

the API running, open a customer with no sign-in, click **Grant sign-in**, confirm the initial
password is shown once and plainly, navigate away and back, confirm it is gone and the section now shows the "already has a sign-in" statement.
